[SWS_CM_00826] Minimum send interval time monitoring for SetHandlers calls by the client
⌈
To protect receivers from flooding/overload, each Set() of the respec-
tive field class shall have a configurable Minimum Send Interval (see ServiceInter-
faceDeploymentElement.minimumSendInterval), which specifies the minimum
amount of time that shall pass between two consecutive calls of SetHandlers by the
client, i.e., the minimum send interval limits the maximum Tx frequency of a given
Set() call for a Field in the network. If the application tries to Field::Set() a field
value, by invoking Set() of the respective field class, ara::com shall check, whether
the time since the last successful handover of the Set() call the underlying transmis-
sion layer is greater than the specified Minimum Send Interval, i.e., the Minimum Send
Interval is not violated. If the Set() handler has never been invoked before, this shall
also successfully pass the minimum send interval check. If the Minimum Send Interval
is not violated, ara::com shall process the Field::Set() call by handing it over
to the transmission layer. The time of handover shall count as start of the new min-
imum send interval monitoring. If the Minimum Send Interval is violated, ara::com
shall discard the Field::Set() call, and return the error code ComErrc::kMini-
mumSendIntervalViolationError (see [SWS_CM_10432]) shall be returned via
the ara::core::Future of the Set() of the respective field class. The Minimum
Send Interval shall only be check on the client side, i.e., by the instance that actually in-
vokes the Field::Set() call and not by the server/provider, which responds/answers
the Field::Set() call. If the configured Minimum Send Interval (ServiceInter-
faceDeploymentElement.minimumSendInterval) of a Set() of the respective
field class has the value 0, the Minimum Send Interval monitoring shall not be active
for the corresponding Field::Set().
⌋
